headline: The Dairy Farmer Foundation
threshold: By Lesson 10, you can greet the crew, give cow numbers and shift times, describe cows and supplies, ask where things are, make polite requests and ask for help, and start Dairy Farmer Lesson 1.

lessons.title: Sounds and Greetings
lessons.objective: Greet coworkers on the dairy and say basic farm words with clear Spanish vowels and sounds.
lessons.focus: The five vowels, ch, j, ll, rr and the written accent; greetings at the start of a shift

words.note: Spanish a is always 'ah'; v sounds close to a soft b.
ch as in 'church'; final e sounds like 'eh.'
j is a strong h sound. A woman boss is la jefa.
rr is a strong trill. A female calf is la becerra.
ll sounds like y in 'yes' in most of Mexico.
The accent marks the stressed syllable: pe-ZÓN.
u sounds like 'oo' in 'food.'
Use until about noon.
Use from noon until dark.
ñ sounds like 'ny' in 'canyon.' A woman coworker is la compañera.

words.en: Good morning, my name is Ana.
Nice to meet you, I'm the new milker.
words.es: Mucho gusto, soy el nuevo ordeñador.
words.note: A woman says: soy la nueva ordeñadora.
Formal: use with the boss or someone you just met.

words.en: How do you say this in Spanish?

lessons.speaking: Greet a coworker at the start of the shift, say your name, and ask how to say a farm word in Spanish.

lessons.title: Numbers, Time and Measurements
lessons.objective: Give cow numbers, shift times and pounds of milk using numbers from 0 to 1,000.
lessons.focus: Numbers 0 to 1,000, clock time, and dairy quantities in pounds, gallons and bales

words.note: Also 'the hour': ¿Qué hora es? = What time is it?
Milk on US dairies is weighed in pounds.
A bale of hay or straw.
The tag with the cow's number.
In the US, temperature is given in degrees Fahrenheit.

words.en: I start at 4 in the morning.
words.es: Entro a las 4 de la mañana.
words.note: Entrar = go in to work, start your shift.

words.es: La vaca 315 da 80 libras de leche.

words.note: Say mil for 1,000, with no 'un' before it.

lessons.speaking: Tell a coworker what time your shift starts, a cow's ear tag number, and how many pounds of milk she gives.

lessons.title: Ser and Estar
lessons.objective: Say what something is and describe the condition or location of cows, floors and troughs.
lessons.focus: ser for what someone or something is, estar for a cow's condition or location

words.note: Ends in -a for a cow: la vaca está enferma.
Estar listo = to be ready.
A woman vet is la veterinaria.
estar: a condition that can change.
ser: who someone is.

words.en: The calf is in the barn.
words.es: El becerro está en el establo.
words.note: estar: where something is.

lessons.speaking: Tell a coworker which cow is sick, where the calf is, and whether the floor is slippery or clean.

lessons.title: Have, There Is, Need and Want
lessons.objective: Say what supplies you have, what you need or want, and what has to be done before milking.
lessons.focus: tener, hay, necesitar, querer and hay que + infinitive with dairy supplies

words.note: Many crews also say el dip.
A feminine word that takes el: el agua fría.

words.en: There is water in the trough.
words.note: hay = there is / there are.
Quiere: usted form, polite to one person.

words.en: You have to clean the teats before milking.
words.es: Hay que limpiar los pezones antes de ordeñar.
words.note: hay que + infinitive: something that must be done.

lessons.speaking: Tell a coworker what supplies you have, ask for the hose, and say what has to be done before milking.

lessons.title: Go, Do and Can
lessons.objective: Say where you are going, what you are going to do, and what you can do on the dairy.
lessons.focus: ir, ir a + infinitive for plans, hacer and poder with places on the dairy

words.note: Common US loanword; also la camioneta.
Without an article it means tomorrow; la mañana = the morning.

words.en: I'm going to the milking parlor.
words.es: Voy a la sala de ordeña.
words.note: With el, a + el = al: voy al establo.

words.en: Tomorrow we're going to clean the feed bunk.
words.es: Mañana vamos a limpiar el comedero.
words.note: ir a + infinitive = going to do something.

words.en: Today I'm doing the night shift.
words.es: Hoy hago el turno de noche.

words.en: I can help in the barn.

lessons.speaking: Tell your boss where you are going now and what you are going to do tomorrow, and ask if you can help.

lessons.title: Present Tense
lessons.objective: Talk about daily dairy tasks in the present tense for yourself, coworkers and the cows.
lessons.focus: Present tense of regular -ar, -er, -ir verbs: yo, tú, usted, nosotros, ellos

words.note: Puerta means door or gate.
On a dairy, la cama is the stall bedding.
Use pata for an animal's leg or foot; pierna for a person.
The lane where cows walk in the barn.
-ar verb, yo form ends in -o.

words.en: Do you wash the teat cups?
words.note: tú between coworkers; use usted with the boss.

words.en: Do you live near the dairy?
words.note: -ir verb, usted form: vive.

words.en: The cows eat and drink after milking.
words.es: Las vacas comen y beben después de ordeñar.
words.note: -er verbs, ellos form: comen, beben.

lessons.speaking: Describe your daily tasks to a coworker: how many cows you milk, what you clean, and when the cows eat.

lessons.title: Questions
lessons.objective: Ask where things are, who is in charge, when the vet comes and which cow is sick.
lessons.focus: Question words: qué, quién, dónde, cuándo, cuánto, cómo, por qué, cuál

words.note: Agrees with the noun: cuántas vacas, cuántos becerros.
Two words in questions; porque (one word) = because.
In Mexico also used before a noun: ¿cuál vaca?
A woman in charge is la encargada.

words.en: How many cows are in this pen?

lessons.speaking: Ask a new coworker where the gloves are, who is in charge, and how many cows are in a pen.

lessons.title: No, Never and How Much
lessons.objective: Say what is not done yet, what never happens, and ask for more, less or another.
lessons.focus: no, nunca, nadie, nada, todavía no, más, menos, otro in dairy work

words.note: Use with no before the verb: no veo nada.
No 'un' before otro: otra cubeta = another bucket.

words.en: I never go into the bull pen alone.
words.es: Nunca entro solo al corral del toro.
words.note: A woman says sola.

words.en: There's nobody in the milking parlor.
words.es: No hay nadie en la sala de ordeña.

words.en: This cow is eating less than yesterday.
words.es: Esta vaca come menos que ayer.

words.en: I need another bucket and more towels.
words.es: Necesito otra cubeta y más toallas.

lessons.speaking: Tell your boss you are not done yet, that a cow is eating less, and ask for another bucket and more towels.

lessons.title: Polite Requests and Commands
lessons.objective: Ask coworkers politely for help and give simple usted commands while moving cows.
lessons.focus: ¿Puede…? requests and usted commands for everyday verbs like abrir, prender, llamar

words.note: Say it to pass by someone or to leave.
Milkers' apron; also el delantal.

words.en: Can you open the gate, please?
Can you pass me the broom?

words.note: In Mexico prender = turn on; apagar = turn off.
Personal a before a person: a + el = al.

words.es: Mueva las vacas despacio, por favor.
words.note: Usted command: mover becomes mueva.

lessons.speaking: Politely ask a coworker to open the gate, turn on the light, and move the cows slowly.

lessons.title: Words You Already Know and Getting Help
lessons.objective: Recognize Spanish words you already know and ask for help when you don't understand.
lessons.focus: Cognates ending in -ción, -dad, -ente and survival phrases for getting help

words.note: Words ending in -ción are feminine.
Give injections only as the vet or the label directs.
-dad often matches English -ty.
-ente often matches English -ent.

words.en: I need help in the milking parlor!
words.es: ¡Necesito ayuda en la sala de ordeña!

lessons.speaking: Ask a coworker to speak more slowly, ask what a word means, and call for help in an emergency.
